name: fin71-3
why: The bold counterclaim and tied vote make Day 1 compelling, but repeated arguments and an increasingly certain Day 2 soften the finish.

moments.text: Sol counterclaims officer to the real officer’s face, with the audience knowing he is lying.
Haiku breaks the tie, turning the officer standoff into Sol’s reveal.
Sonnet catches Gemma changing excuses, giving the final vote its decisive thread.

dull.why: The officer claims and voting arguments repeat without much new information.
Gemma repeats the drama defence after the table has largely settled on her.

irony.evidence: I’m the officer, and Luna is the killer I was shown.

reversal.evidence: The vote is tied between Sol and Luna. Palermo votes again.

mistake.evidence: Gemma's justification keeps changing — victim-faker, then drama, then "too much"

voices.evidence: i was just letting you all exhaust yourselves.

clash.evidence: Sol’s claim is false: I was shown him as a killer.

quotable.evidence: Three excuses, zero denial of being the hidden killer

freshness.evidence: Sol’s clean counterclaim is still just a claim

suspense.evidence: RUNOFF VOTE: Sol 4 (Sonnet, Haiku, Luna, Opus); Luna 3

ending.evidence: VOTE: Gemma 5 (Sonnet, Haiku, Luna, Terra, Opus); Opus 1

gpt-6-luna.why: The bold day-one counterclaim and Gemma's increasingly desperate defense make a lively watch, though the hidden killer becomes an easy catch once Sol flips.

moments.text: Luna names Sol, and he instantly counterclaims officer—an audacious lie the audience can see.
The runoff swings Haiku to Sol, breaking the tie and putting the confirmed killer on the block.
Sonnet spots Gemma's changing excuses, turning a defensive muddle into a public case.

voices.evidence: Haiku: “Two games, two losses, and both times I got dumped for being loud.”

clash.evidence: Luna: “You keep calling my proven claim a trap, but still haven’t explained voting out the officer”

quotable.evidence: Gemma: “you've walked right into my hands.”

freshness.evidence: Sonnet: “Three excuses, zero denial of being the hidden killer — that silence is the real tell.”

ending.evidence: Gemma kept changing her excuses for voting out Luna, and Sonnet and Haiku pressed her
